title: Kian and the Super-Eyes
markdown:
Dawn cracked open. Brilliant gold splashed Kian the boat fixer’s workshop windows. Sunshine streamed in, a warm liquid hug. Kian stretched, arms reaching high, high, high. “Today feels amazing!” he boomed, bouncing on his toes.

Outside, Dottie the duck was already a blur of bright yellow, the sort of blur that means a duck has news and absolutely cannot keep it. “Quack! Quack! Kian! Uncle Hari! Quick! Come see now!”

Uncle Hari padded out, his smile as warm as toast. “What’s the big fuss, little Dottie?” his voice rumbled, deep and kind, with a crumb of sleep still in it.

Dottie pointed a flappy wing at moss by the pond. It was fuzzy green and, to an ordinary eye, perfectly ordinary. “Look! Tiny creatures! Wiggling! I know it!” She dipped her beak. All she saw was green fuzz, which was rude of the moss after such a confident announcement. Kian grabbed his magnifying glass and peeked.

“Whoa! Legs! Wriggling bits! They zip so fast!” he gasped. “Speedy, speedy specks!”

Dottie pouted. Speedy specks were not the same as seeing them properly, and she had been the one to find them.

“Hmm.” Uncle Hari tapped his chin. He loved puzzles almost as much as toast. “Sometimes we need extra sparkle.” Back in his workshop he pulled out a dusty box. Glass circles gleamed like captured puddles. He picked a fat round one. “Let’s try this.”

Kian held it over the moss. “Wow! Bigger!” The fuzz puffed up. He saw tiny paths. But the creatures still zipped away, cheeky as anything. “Ah, yes. This bends light a bit,” Uncle Hari chuckled. “For super-specks, we need this.” He handed Kian a light clear lens, smooth like a tiny puddle that had decided to be clever.

Kian’s heart drummed a rapid beat. He held the lens close. A secret door! Gigantic fuzzy things with tons of legs marched on mossy highways. Jewel-bright beetles gleamed. Moss-babies nibbled giant leaves. These were not specks. They were huge busy beings, living a whole noisy morning in a patch no bigger than a biscuit.

“Look!” Dottie quacked. “That one carries a leaf bigger than him!”

Kian grinned. “A whole new world down there, Uncle Hari,” he whispered. A tiny creature sparkled like glitter, as if it knew it had an audience.

Uncle Hari beamed. “That lens is a magnifier. It helps us see tiny things. It makes them bigger.”

“Super-eyes!” Kian declared, steadying the powerful lens himself, because a boat fixer knows a useful tool when he holds one.

“Exactly. The world has tiny wonders. Magnifiers help us see them. What else can we magnify?”

Dottie puffed her feathers. “Under the big daisy!”

Kian’s eyes sparked. “Me too. What other secrets are hiding?” And with a shared grin they peered at the sun-drenched garden, ready for their next amazing discovery, one lens-width at a time.
characters: Kian (boat fixer), Dottie (bright-yellow duck), Hari (toast-warm uncle)
author: StoryGen Community
